(April 6, 2026) – Poynting crater and Keeler crater are visible side by side in the lower right portion of this image of the Moon’s far side highlands. Poynting, positioned above, is a large impact crater with a well-defined rim and relatively smooth interior, indicative of material that has settled following the initial impact. Just below it, Keeler crater appears slightly smaller, with a sharply outlined rim and a more textured interior shaped by subsequent impacts and ejecta. Both features lie within the densely cratered far side highlands, preserving a record of ancient impacts that have shaped the lunar surface over billions of years.

Category 5 Hurricane Melissa, one of the most powerful storms to strike the Caribbean in recent history, is pictured about 50 miles south of Jamaica in this photograph from the International Space Station as it orbited 262 miles above the Yucatan Peninsula.

<h2 class="wp-block-heading">America’s newest and most exciting aerospace technology expo and air show</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Celebrate the spirit of American innovation at NASA MAX POWER — an exposition of air and space technologies at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, Nov. 7-8. The two-day event will feature immersive experiences for all ages to enjoy, including NASA air shows, technology demonstrations, spaceflight hardware, military aircraft, and behind‑the‑scenes access to America’s spaceport. Attend talks led by NASA experts and meet astronauts from some of agency’s most famous missions!</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In collaboration with Air Dot Show, UP.Summit, Space Florida, Delaware North, and Purpose Entertainment, MAX POWER blends history, exploration, and the cutting edge of aerospace into an unforgettable experience.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In honor of America’s historic 250th anniversary, NASA and external collaborators are hosting MAX POWER, a two-day aerospace festival celebrating the past, present, and future of flight and space exploration. <p class="wp-block-paragraph">The event will take place Nov. 7 -8, and activities will span NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida including the Apollo Saturn V facility, and the Launch and Landing Facility currently leased by Space Florida. <p class="wp-block-paragraph">MAX POWER is organized into three park experiences. Presented by Air Dot Show, park one is a multi-day air show featuring military aircraft and flyovers by NASA, the Department of War, and the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds. In park two, presented by UP.Summit, experience a hands-on technology showcase of futuristic aircraft, drones, autonomous vehicles, and more mobility innovations. Park three includes an all-access pass to the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex exhibits and attractions and behind-the-gates tours of NASA’s Kennedy Space Center. Choose your own adventure —each park offers a unique experience. Attend one, two, or all three!</p>

POWER Home Get Tickets Frequently Asked Questions America’s newest and most exciting aerospace technology expo and air show Celebrate the spirit of American innovation at NASA MAX POWER — an exposition of air and space technologies at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, Nov. 7-8. The two-day event will feature immersive experiences for all ages to enjoy, including NASA air shows, technology demonstrations, spaceflight hardware, military aircraft, and behind‑the‑scenes access to America’s spaceport. Attend talks led by NASA experts and meet astronauts from some of agency’s most famous missions! In collaboration with Air Dot Show, UP.Summit, Space Florida, Delaware North, and Purpose Entertainment, MAX POWER blends history, exploration, and the cutting edge of aerospace into an unforgettable experience. What to expect Air Shows See planes soar Tech Showcase Envision the future Astronauts Meet the explorers And More… Experience America's spaceport Get Your Tickets to MAX POWER MAX POWER is organized into three park experiences. Separate ticketing for each park enables visitors to customize their visit to best fit their interests and schedule. Attend one, two, or all three! Park descriptions and links to purchase tickets are available below. Links to external sites are provided for informational purposes and do not imply NASA’s endorsement. Air Dot Show Presented by Air Dot Show, park one will feature thrilling, multi-day air shows featuring military aircraft and flyovers by NASA, the Department of War, the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds, and more! Get Tickets UP.Summit Presented by UP.Summit, in park two you can explore the latest innovations in transportation. From autonomous vehicles to cutting-edge drones and space exploration technologies, come and see what the future holds! Get Tickets Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex Park three includes an all-access pass to the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex exhibits and attractions and behind-the-gates tours of NASA’s Kennedy Space Center, home to America's historic launch facilities. Get Tickets max power Celebrate American Leadership in Air and Space Technology Experience the best of American aeronautics and space technology! In honor of America’s 250th birthday, MAX POWER will pay homage to our remarkable past, explore current missions, and lay a foundation for our nation’s future endeavors: from Earth to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Join us Frequently Asked Questions What is MAX POWER? In honor of America’s historic 250th anniversary, NASA and external collaborators are hosting MAX POWER, a two-day aerospace festival celebrating the past, present, and future of flight and space exploration. The event will feature air shows, cutting-edge technology showcases, and immersive space exhibits to create an unforgettable experience. When and where will the event take place? The event will take place Nov. 7 -8, and activities will span NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida including the Apollo Saturn V facility, and the Launch and Landing Facility currently leased by Space Florida. Other activities will take place at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex adjacent to the center.  Who should attend MAX POWER? The two-day event includes a range of experiences for students, families, aerospace and technology enthusiasts, industry partners, and NASA fans of all ages to discover, learn, and be inspired. What types of activities can attendees expect? Programming includes interactive exhibits and talks with NASA experts, tours of NASA’s Kennedy Space Center, live technology demonstrations, air shows with aircraft flyovers, astronaut meetups, and more! See the full event schedule to plan your experience. The event is divided into three parks, how does that work? MAX POWER is organized into three park experiences. Presented by Air Dot Show, park one is a multi-day air show featuring military aircraft and flyovers by NASA, the Department of War, and the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds. In park two, presented by UP.Summit, experience a hands-on technology showcase of futuristic aircraft, drones, autonomous vehicles, and more mobility innovations. Park three includes an all-access pass to the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex exhibits and attractions and behind-the-gates tours of NASA’s Kennedy Space Center. Choose your own adventure —each park offers a unique experience. Attend one, two, or all three! Are tickets required, and is there a cost to attend? Yes, tickets are required to access each MAX POWER theme park. Separate ticketing for each park enables visitors to customize their experience to best fit their interests and schedule. Park tickets are available for purchase by following the links on the MAX POWER event page. Why do I need to purchase tickets through another website? Shouldn’t this event be free? To make the production of this event possible, NASA is working with external collaborators, including Air Dot Show, Space Florida, UP.Summit, Delaware North, and Purpose Entertainment. Because the event relies on the funding and structure provided by these external organizations rather than exclusively using NASA’s federally appropriated budget, ticketing is handled through their external sites so they can cover their costs of producing the event. How can I stay updated? To help plan your visit, we will soon release the official MAX POWER event app. You can also email us at: maxpower@mail.nasa.gov . Can I collaborate to support this event? You may contact nasa-brand-partnerships@mail.nasa.gov with inquiries about collaboration opportunities. How do members of the media or digital content creators cover the event? This in-person event is open to U.S. media and digital content creators . Media and creators must apply to attend MAX POWER at https://media.ksc.nasa.gov/ by the deadline established by NASA’s Office of Communications. NASA’s media accreditation policy is available online. (April 6, 2026) – Poynting crater and Keeler crater are visible side by side in the lower right portion of this image of the Moon’s far side highlands. Poynting, positioned above, is a large impact crater with a well-defined rim and relatively smooth interior, indicative of material that has settled following the initial impact. Just below it, Keeler crater appears slightly smaller, with a sharply outlined rim and a more textured interior shaped by subsequent impacts and ejecta. Both features lie within the densely cratered far side highlands, preserving a record of ancient impacts that have shaped the lunar surface over billions of years.

Category 5 Hurricane Melissa, one of the most powerful storms to strike the Caribbean in recent history, is pictured about 50 miles south of Jamaica in this photograph from the International Space Station as it orbited 262 miles above the Yucatan Peninsula.

<h3 class="wp-block-heading">The air traffic solutions NASA is working on today builds from a foundation of research that goes back decades. Three projects concluded a few years ago in particular are helping to develop new ways of doing things today in the 21st century. The two features presented here help tell those project’s stories.</h3>

Read this Story About NASA’s Air Traffic Solutions As NASA Aeronautics senior writer Jim Banke tells his grandson, Axel, about two recently concluded research projects involving drones large and small, Axel appears to be imagining what the major elements of that future as told to him by his grandpa might be. (April 6, 2026) – Poynting crater and Keeler crater are visible side by side in the lower right portion of this image of the Moon’s far side highlands. Poynting, positioned above, is a large impact crater with a well-defined rim and relatively smooth interior, indicative of material that has settled following the initial impact. Just below it, Keeler crater appears slightly smaller, with a sharply outlined rim and a more textured interior shaped by subsequent impacts and ejecta. Both features lie within the densely cratered far side highlands, preserving a record of ancient impacts that have shaped the lunar surface over billions of years.

Category 5 Hurricane Melissa, one of the most powerful storms to strike the Caribbean in recent history, is pictured about 50 miles south of Jamaica in this photograph from the International Space Station as it orbited 262 miles above the Yucatan Peninsula.

								</div>
																													<p class="p-md">For more than 65 years, NASA has made the seemingly impossible, possible. We conduct cutting-edge research to advance technology and aeronautics. We operate the world’s leading space laboratory, the International Space Station, and will establish a sustainable and strong exploration presence on the Moon this decade through the Artemis campaign.</p>

															<div class="margin-bottom-2">
									<h2 class="heading-29">Looking Forward</h2>
								</div>
																													<p class="p-md">NASA’s future will continue to be a story of human exploration, technology, and science. We will go back to the Moon to learn more about what it will take to support human exploration to Mars and beyond. We will continue to nurture the development of a vibrant low-Earth orbit economy that builds on the work done to date by the International Space Station. NASA engineers will develop new technologies to improve air transport at home and meet the challenges of advanced space exploration. Our scientists will work to increase an understanding of our planet and our place in the universe.</p>

								</div>
																													<p class="p-md">When NASA opened for business on October 1, 1958, it accelerated the work already started on human and robotic spaceflight, and over the last 65 years it has continued to push the boundaries of aeronautics and space exploration. NASA Today Looking Forward A History of Innovation NASA Today For more than 65 years, NASA has made the seemingly impossible, possible. At its 20 centers and facilities across the country and with U.S. commercial companies and international partners, NASA leads studying Earth science, including climate, our Sun, solar system, and the larger universe. We conduct cutting-edge research to advance technology and aeronautics. We operate the world’s leading space laboratory, the International Space Station, and will establish a sustainable and strong exploration presence on the Moon this decade through the Artemis campaign. NASA Centers and Facilities Technicians inside the Payload Hazardous Servicing Facility at Kennedy Space Center in Florida install and test antennas on a solar array on Wednesday, March 20, 2024, for the agency’s Europa Clipper spacecraft. NASA/Isaac Watson Looking Forward NASA’s future will continue to be a story of human exploration, technology, and science. We will go back to the Moon to learn more about what it will take to support human exploration to Mars and beyond. We will continue to nurture the development of a vibrant low-Earth orbit economy that builds on the work done to date by the International Space Station. NASA engineers will develop new technologies to improve air transport at home and meet the challenges of advanced space exploration. Our scientists will work to increase an understanding of our planet and our place in the universe. NASA Missions The Artemis II crew, from left: NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch; CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen; and NASA astronaut Victor Glover pose for a group photo after viewing the Orion spacecraft in the well deck of the USS John P. Murtha, Saturday, April 11, 2026, in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California. NASA/Bill Ingalls A History of Innovation When NASA opened for business on October 1, 1958, it accelerated the work already started on human and robotic spaceflight, and over the last 65 years it has continued to push the boundaries of aeronautics and space exploration. Now NASA is preparing to take humankind farther than ever before, as it helps to foster a robust commercial space economy near Earth, and pioneers further human and robotic exploration as we venture into deep space. NASA History NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover took a selfie with the Ingenuity helicopter, seen here about 13 feet from the rover. This image was taken by the WASTON camera on the rover’s robotic arm on April 6, 2021, the 46th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS NASA Leadership Administrator Jared Isaacman Jared “Rook” Isaacman is the 15th Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. An entrepreneur and skilled pilot, Isaacman commanded Inspiration4, the first all-civilian orbital spaceflight aboard the Dragon spacecraft. The mission was a major milestone in commercial spaceflight. Full Biography Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson Matt Anderson is NASA’s deputy administrator. Anderson is a decorated Air Force command pilot in multiple aircraft with more than 5,000 flight hours, including more than 650 in combat. Throughout his 24-year Air Force career, he served on several senior U.S. Department of War staffs and commanded at multiple levels before retiring in 2021. Full Biography Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya Amit Kshatriya is NASA’s associate administrator. Kshatriya serves as the highest-ranking civil servant at the agency and as a senior advisor to the administrator. Kshatriya leads the agency’s 10 center directors, as well as the mission directorate associate administrators at NASA Headquarters in Washington. (April 6, 2026) – Poynting crater and Keeler crater are visible side by side in the lower right portion of this image of the Moon’s far side highlands. Poynting, positioned above, is a large impact crater with a well-defined rim and relatively smooth interior, indicative of material that has settled following the initial impact. Just below it, Keeler crater appears slightly smaller, with a sharply outlined rim and a more textured interior shaped by subsequent impacts and ejecta. Both features lie within the densely cratered far side highlands, preserving a record of ancient impacts that have shaped the lunar surface over billions of years.

Category 5 Hurricane Melissa, one of the most powerful storms to strike the Caribbean in recent history, is pictured about 50 miles south of Jamaica in this photograph from the International Space Station as it orbited 262 miles above the Yucatan Peninsula.

Kit de prensa de la misión Artemis II Ciencia de la NASA Space Place para niños Aeronáutica de la NASA Ciencia de la NASA Para todos La ciencia es la clave para descubrir los secretos del universo: uniendo a la humanidad con cada descubrimiento, expandiendo nuestro conocimiento y despertando nuestra imaginación. Al navegar por las arenas del tiempo y el espacio, la ciencia da contexto y significado a mediciones grandes y pequeñas. ¿Sabías que existen tantas estrellas en el universo como hay granos de arena en la Tierra? La nueva era de los descubrimientos científicos de la NASA acaba de comenzar, ¡y tú eres parte de ella! Lee más Space Place Para niños El galardonado sitio web Space Place de la NASA atrae a los niños de primaria superior a las ciencias espaciales y terrestres a través de juegos interactivos, actividades prácticas, artículos divertidos y videos cortos. Con material en inglés y español y numerosos recursos para niños, padres y maestros, Space Place tiene algo para todos. Lee más Aeronáutica de la NASA Para todos Gracias a los avances tecnológicos desarrollados por la NASA, la industria de la aviación está mejor equipada que nunca para transportar a pasajeros y carga de manera segura y eficiente a destinos en todo el mundo. De hecho, todos los aviones estadounidenses que vuelan hoy día, así como todos los controles de tráfico aéreo de los Estados Unidos, utilizan, de alguna manera u otra, tecnología desarrollada por la NASA. (April 6, 2026) – Poynting crater and Keeler crater are visible side by side in the lower right portion of this image of the Moon’s far side highlands. Poynting, positioned above, is a large impact crater with a well-defined rim and relatively smooth interior, indicative of material that has settled following the initial impact. Just below it, Keeler crater appears slightly smaller, with a sharply outlined rim and a more textured interior shaped by subsequent impacts and ejecta. Both features lie within the densely cratered far side highlands, preserving a record of ancient impacts that have shaped the lunar surface over billions of years.
